# Checkpoint 9 — cumulative reconciliation, hardening and qualification

## Disposition

The cumulative native-widget candidate is implemented and delivered, not a recommendations-only review. Expanded qualification remains **PARTIAL**: the mandatory loaded CPU1/CPU×4 response, accelerated-preview availability and actual target-platform/deployment gates are not fulfilled. The final checkpoint remains 9; the attached implementation DAG is the continuation, not another checkpoint. A fresh verification receipt beside the ZIP is authoritative for the exact final-byte run. Counts and measurements inside this report explicitly distinguish pre-seal variants from final extraction.

## Implemented corrections and justified improvements

**Elevation ownership (CP8-F01).** CP8.3 still read a shared unowned `siteElev`. Eight tests reproduced incorrect successor ownership. A finite elevation is now bound to the accepted target generation/coordinates and eligible native weather; stale/missing/unowned values become labelled zero-height assumptions, distinct from legitimately admitted zero. An exact additive notification follows native weather admission. A→B→A, late callbacks, missing/stale/simulated weather, subsequent B and known-zero states are tested in hooks and actual native adoption. Existing native admission code is unchanged apart from that explicit notification.

**Currentness (CP8-F02).** CP8.3 already had independent invalidation epochs, latest work coalescing, native-clock discontinuity, hidden/dispose and publication fences. Those were retained and the original's 30-second maximum accepted-UTC age adopted. Normal refresh is still four seconds. Forced seeks, wall-clock jumps, target/source generations and obsolete completion are exercised. Passing stale-safety is distinct from high-rate availability, which remains open.

**Worker-failure policy (CP8-F03).** Actual 8.3 synchronous fallback blocked a 16 ms heartbeat for 2255.5 ms and delayed a dialog action 2106.2 ms. The selected donor-style physical-stage withdrawal reduced the matched failure gap to 17.8 ms while retaining prayer/calendar interaction. Worker constructor/post/decode/exception/deadline failures, explicit retry and restoration are tested. No physical job runs synchronously as a worker-loss fallback. This trades absent optional sky on worker-disabled deployments for responsive essential UI; it does not automatically qualify all normal-mode cost.

**Additional donor safeguards.** Reversible generation-fenced pagehide suspension was adopted, with persisted-only pageshow restoration after a reproduced startup-event ordering failure. Native physical jobs reject a second cloud transmission/glow owner. An additive compact realSky QA join preserves existing fields and labels obsolete synthetic counters. Portable explicit browser selection was implemented without silently substituting missing engines.

**Scintillation contract.** The prior `{enabled:false}` option was ignored by the actual retained scientific function, which uses `strength`. The intended disable is now `strength:0`, avoiding an unintended 0.73/1.17 Hz effect sampled at four-second physical updates. Native cloud motion is not disabled. Smooth optional stellar scintillation is not fabricated as an implemented feature or a mandatory remediation node.

**Exact measured presentation optimisation.** CPU profiling identified repeated native DOMMatrix getter access and loop-invariant antialias width inside every Moon-mask pixel. Hoisting six coefficients and the ramp preserves every sample in 48 affine/radius/DPR combinations. The matched actual native transform median fell from 12.75 ms to 1.4 ms; moved and sheared controls are also exact. Original failing control and benchmark-harness failure are preserved.

The donor's cloud-pixel equality shortcut was adapted rather than copied: a skip also requires identical physical frame, old/new foreground support, calendar geometry and native PBR bytes. A real browser test found that an identical-pixel skip left source metadata stale; this was repaired and the failed/passing controls retained. No opacity, cadence, physics resolution, sky field or data tier was reduced to obtain these optimisations.

## One coherent composition policy

The runtime retains the 325×530 perspective camera (south 180°, altitude 45°, vertical FOV90°, roll 0°, physical DPR 1), E24 nominal pre-foreground meter, native inverse-shared-tone material/colour interpretation, T=1−A from the actual cloud painter after its original blur/support and local-light assumption 0.003×lp before native foreground. These are declared presentations/assumptions, not newly calibrated measurements.

At each pixel, gas-transported atmospheric background S and physically occulted direct stellar/diffuse D form S+D×calendarMask. Native PBR material then composes using its own alpha, followed by native cloud colour/transmission once, then the shared encode once. The physical Moon and enlarged calendar display remain different semantic owners. Native Sun/discrete optics, precipitation and prayer/readability DOM layers remain native presentations; the whole DOM is not claimed as one radiometrically calibrated framebuffer.

The original's `(1−A)^k` cloud calibration, different colour radiance scale/cloud-aware exposure,325×216 camera at 25°/95°, E2,0.005×lp² outside-cloud local light and physical lunar preview overrides were compared, not imported incidentally. On identical transported fields, same exposure, no native colour/local addition and matched transmissions 0/.08/.5/1, both equations yield identical encoded pixels. Under native colour/meter policies, the retained fixture differs by up to64 code values. This identifies incompatible semantics, not a measured physical winner. Six actual native night/cloud/day views—both implementations with their own declared defaults—are retained separately.

## Qualification performed and its scope

The integration suite grew as the exact mask/cache corrections were added; the final readable/runtime suite contains **97** passing integration tests. The final complete suite is rerun from the sealed extraction rather than borrowing old counts. The pre-seal full affected campaign passed 849 applicable native regressions across 26 commands, 305 scientific JavaScript and 117 scientific Python cases, 15 actual-widget scenes with 88 assertions, 19 lifecycle/failure cases with 386 assertions and four new native controls with 87 assertions. All of these are required again in the final verifier.

The actual material control preserves 8,044 opaque native lunar samples exactly. The moved-Moon full-frame equation compares 172,250 pixels / 516,750 channels with zero differences and detects deliberately wrong attenuation/colour/order. Native moving-cloud, mask and dirty-input controls retain changing actual pixels; freezing the foreground is not a performance fix. The final verification receipt supplies the last-run numbers.

The broader native matrix has 43 cases: Florida/Madinah/Reykjavík/Sydney × January/April/July/October × local late-night/noon (32), display DPR 1/1.37/2/3 (4), plus seven camera/polar/horizon/strict-support cases. Seasonal observations are fixed declared fixtures, not live weather or new astronomical source acquisition. CSS displayDPR changes do not turn the fixed physical DPR 1 raster into high-resolution physics. The test keeps numeric state, source support and error checks alongside screenshots.

Retained independent astrometric and Sun/Moon oracle fixtures were rerun without changing the scientific snapshot. The inherited Sun maximum 0.00869317° and Moon maximum 0.08789242° directional differences remain within their declared existing model budgets; exact lunar contacts are not certified. This is a rerun against retained independent reference values, not fresh upstream ephemeris acquisition.

Eight explicit asset restarts retain one live worker, Blob URL and raster; disposal releases all three. The main-JS-heap growth test meets its 8 MiB bound. It does not measure total worker/GPU/process/backing-store memory. Six isolated lifecycle/source negative variants are detected. Twenty-two Python tests validate the explicit browser selector, evidence/DAG integrity and qualifier verdict distinctions; structural DAG PASS does not close any implementation node.

## What remains unresolved

**CP9-N001 — loaded responsiveness.** The retained pre-seal normal-CPU trials passed the declared 250ms heartbeat/dialog budget, but the full fresh-extraction rerun did not reproduce an all-pass result. Its five full-motion heartbeat maxima at CPU1 were 136.8/72.3/276.8/75.0/104.9ms; reduced-motion maxima were 223.1/239.5/264.8/161.0/79.5ms. CPU×4 full-motion maxima were 418.9/318.5/651.0/673.4/719.9ms, with one scheduled-dialog lag of 1012.9ms. CPU×4 reduced motion also exceeded the budget. The native baseline itself failed three of five CPU×4 trials, so not all cost is attributed to the sky. The final-source CPU profile still shows substantial linearToSrgb/encodeFrame/nativeForeground/getImageData work over its explicitly recorded sample interval. It is diagnostic attribution, not an additive total or a real mobile benchmark. The separate fresh receipt/evidence retains every trial; neither occasional CPU1 failures nor throttled failures were discarded or rerun away.

**CP9-N002 — accelerated availability.** At 60×/600× the retained 10-second run accepts zero new moving frames because the clock outruns the allowed render age; 10× has visibility gaps. No stale sky is published and frozen recovery is current. A 1× first transition takes time, but visibility after its first accepted frame is continuous. The test's>=2 new frames and>=80% visible-sample target is a declared CP9 stress target, not retroactively an inherited native promise. It is not passed. Explicit unsupported-rate status would improve honesty but cannot alone qualify continuous playback; the DAG states the actual throughput objective and prohibits relaxing the 30-second fence.

**CP9-N003 — actual-platform/deployment acceptance.** The actual widget was executed under Linux Chromium with controlled providers/date and embedded/subresource routes. Local HTTP/file top-level navigation was attempted and blocked by administrator policy. Firefox/WebKit were not installed successfully; there is no native Windows or live-provider/BFCache/deployment pass. Browser launch, portable invocation, synthetic persisted events and DPR emulation do not substitute for this evidence. The DAG defines the hash-bound collector and exact tests for a suitable runner.

The remaining scientific source limitations—V-equivalent diffuse light, conservative exclusions/estimates, sparse target spectra, assumed atmosphere/night/local light, coarse Moon model and screen-space cloud presentation—remain explicit. No unsupported cosmetic or research work is invented just to fill the graph.
